full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the plaintiff has arisen out of a judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd, Court, Dhaka reversing those of the learned Munsif, 6th Court Dhaka, passed in a suit for permanent injunction to restrain the defendants from constructing the building beyond the approved plan and for mandatory injunction for demolishing of the building constructed beyond the plan. 

 4. The learned Munsif decreed the suit. He has found that the defendant's plea that they have some lands beyond the boundary wall is baseless and vague. He has also held that the defendants have not kept 4' feet space from the boundary wall between the land of the plaintiff and the defendants. The learned Munsif has observed that the defendant No. 2 (D.W.1) has admitted that distance between their construction and the disputed boundary wall is 1 foot to 2 feet 8/9 inches from south to north. 

 On appeal the court of appeal below has reversed the decision of the trial court and dismissed the suit upon view that the plaintiff is not entitled to a decree as he has not acquired easement right over the land of the defendants requiring the latter to keep 4 feet space between their construction and the disputed boundary wall. He has also held that if there is any violation of the Building Construction Laws and Rules the D.I.T. can take action under section 187 of the Town Improvement Act. The Court of appeal below has found as follows: 

 "From the evidence on record it appears that the plaintiff and the defendants are the owners of their respective purchased land and they have been in possession of their purchased land as such the plaintiff cannot get any decree for mandatory injunction for the alleged violation of the Building Construction Rules inasmuch as there has been no breach of obligation existing in favour of the plaintiff. Moreover, no right of easement of the air and light accrued in favour of the plaintiff." 

 5. Mr. Jamiruddin Sircar the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff has firstly submitted that the defendants being obliged under law to keep vacant 4 feet space i.e. 9 meter at the back of their constructions from the common boundary wall and admittedly a space of only 1 foot to 9", inch having been left by the defendants in between the boundary wall and their constructions and this being clearly violative of the provision for the building construction Act and the Rules there under, the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law occasioning a failure of justice in holding that the plaintiff has not succeeded in proving his legal right requiring the defendants to keep a vacant space as alleged by the plaintiff. The learned Advocate has next submitted that in view of the provision of Building Construction Act and the Rules there under the plaintiff has acquired a right requiring defendants to keep a vacant space of 4 feet from the boundary wall, and the learned Subordinate Judge on misconception of law as to the rights and obligations of the adjoining shares of land with respect to construction of Building in urban areas, has committed an error in reversing the judgment of the trial court upon a view that the plaintiff cannot get a decree for alleged violation of Building Construction Rules. He has next submitted that by virtue of provision of section 7 read with sections 32 and 35 of the Easement Act the defendants are obliged under the law to keep some vacant space in between his building and the wall. He has further submitted that apart from acquisition of right of easement by prescription, under the Building Construction Act, 1952 and the Rules thereunder a legal obligation on the part of the defendants vis-a-vis a right in favour of the plaintiff has accrued inasmuch as that the defendants have to keep a vacant space of 4 feet from the comma boundary wall and as per the plan passed by the D.I.T. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff has lastly submitted that the defendants having committed tortious wrong in not keeping 4 feet space between wall and their building, the latter are liable not to proceed with the construction and to pull down their construction already made in violation of the plan and the Building Construction Rules. The learned Advocate has further submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice in holding that the D.I T. having not taken any action against the defendants for making construction in violation of the plan and the Building Construction Rules the plaintiff is not entitled to maintain the action for injunction and demolition of the unauthorised construction. 

 6. Mr. T. H Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant opposite party has submitted that the plaintiff has acquired no easement right either under the provisions of Easement Act or under the provision of Building Construction Act 1952 and the Rules thereunder inasmuch as the plaintiff has not acquired any easement by prescription or under sections 7, 32 or 35 of the Easement Act as claimed by the latter. Elaborating his submission he has argued that the provision of sec. 7 of Easement Act is descriptive of several modes or classes of Easement Act and that the said provision has not created any right by easement. He has further submitted that the plaintiff has not acquired any legal right or right of action even if it is found that the defendant has made construction in violation of the Building Rules or of the plan sanctioned by the D.I.T. The learned Advocate has further submitted that the laws governing construction of building in urban areas under the Building Construction Act, 1952 or under Town Improvement Act, 1953, do not give an adjoining owners of a property any right of action in case of violation of the Building Construction Rules under the Building Construction Act 1953, or the approved plan as passed by D.I.T. The learned Advocate has next submitted that by special law, namely, Town Improvement Act penalties having been provided for violation of building construction rules or violation of sanctioned plan, the adjoining owners have no right to an injunction or demolision of any structure constructed in violation of the rules or the plan. According to the learned Advocate, special provisions in the aforesaid laws as regards penalty and punishments for violation of the Building Construction Rules having been provided any action at the instance of the plaintiff for an injunction or any mandatory injunction to demolish any structure would not lie. According to the learned Advocate variation of the building construction plan or the Rules has not given a right to the plaintiff to sue to restrain the defendants from making any construction in violation of the sanctioned plan or of the Rules. He has further submitted that the plaintiff having not sought relief by way of declaration of his right of easement over the defendants land no decree for permanent injunction or mandatory injunction could be legally given. In support of the case of the respective parties they have cited decision reported in A. I. R. 1952 Calcutta 74, A.T.R. 1936 Madrass 142 and A.I,R. 1943 Oudh 111. 

 13. In the result this Rule succeeds and it is accordingly made absolute. The judgment and decree of the court of appeal below is set aside, and those of the trial court are modified to the effect that the plaintiff shall get a decree of Tk. 10,000.00 as compensation instead of permanent injunction to restrain the defendants from making further construction and mandatory injunction by way of demolishing of the existing structure. The suit is, therefore, remanded back to the trial court for the purpose of passing a decree for Tk. 10,000.00 in favour of the plaintiff on receipt of requisite court fee on the amount aforesaid. If the plaintiff fails to put in the requisites court fee within three months from the date of arrival of the records in the trial court, the suit shall stand dismissed. The order granting status quo with respect of the land and constructions of the defendants are vacated. There will be no order as to costs of this Rule.
